practice: Because blood is collected by several organizations, each reports on its own inventory. America's Blood Centers notes that its national data reflects trends and that a local blood center's needs may differ. In July 2026 the American Red Cross reported its supply by blood type, saying it had less than a one-day national supply of type O positive.

publisher.value: Non-government blood organizations, each for its own inventory. America's Blood Centers (an association of community blood centers) publishes a national Daily Inventory Report on the 59 community blood centers; the American Red Cross (a nonprofit that supplies about 40% of the nation's blood) monitors its own national supply daily.

sources.name: America's Blood Centers (non-government): Current U.S. Blood Supply, Daily Inventory Report widget
American Red Cross (nonprofit): American Red Cross Declares Second-Ever National Blood Supply Crisis (July 27, 2026)

unit.value: Days of supply: how many days a center's stock would meet normal demand, which America's Blood Centers groups as 3 or more days, 2 days, or a day or less. The American Red Cross also gives days of supply by blood type, such as less than a one-day supply of type O positive in July 2026.

shortage-threshold.value: America's Blood Centers (non-government) says centers with 3 or more days can meet normal demand, a 2-day supply is running low, and a day or less is critically low.
